evidence: createProduct calls this.createProductService.execute(dto) and returns { id }. This is transport mapping only.
getProducts and getProduct build GetProductsQuery / GetProductQuery and send them through queryBus.execute. No filtering or business logic happens in the controller.
updateProduct, changeStatus and deleteProduct each hand off to the matching application service. There are no status-transition rules or other domain checks in the file.
The only framework concerns are NestJS decorators (@Controller, @Get, @Post, @HttpCode), which belong to the infrastructure/presentation layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The controller sits in the infrastructure layer (presentation/transport) and only does transport work. It maps HTTP routes, path parameters, query parameters and request bodies to application use-case services, or to queries sent through the QueryBus. It also sets HTTP status codes and shapes responses. It contains no business rules, validation logic, domain decisions or persistence code: every method hands off to an application service or query handler.
